sources.title: Is YouTube Studio Down? Issues Persist March 30 2026 as Creators Report Analytics and App Glitches
passages: YouTube Studio, the essential dashboard for millions of content creators worldwide, faced scattered access problems and functionality glitches on Monday, March 30, 2026, with users reporting difficulties viewing analytics, subscriber counts and loading certain sections of the mobile app and web interface.As of early afternoon Pacific time, multiple creators took to social media platforms including X to complain that the YouTube Studio app displayed incomplete data, error messages or failed to load tabs properly.

In previous cases, such as the global YouTube disruption on February 17, 2026, the platform attributed problems to backend systems including recommendation algorithms before confirming resolutions within hours.Creators rely heavily on YouTube Studio for daily operations.

Web access to studio.youtube.com showed mixed results, with some creators able to log in normally while others encountered loading delays or missing real-time statistics.This latest round of complaints follows a pattern of YouTube Studio instability earlier in 2026.
Similar glitches were reported in isolated Reddit threads and creator communities in mid-March.YouTube has not issued an official statement specifically addressing Monday's reports as of press time.

For smaller channels and full-time creators, even brief outages can create stress, especially when real-time analytics are unavailable during peak viewing hours.Monday's issues appeared less severe than the March 10 event, which affected loading across both mobile and desktop for many users simultaneously.

Geographic distribution of complaints suggested possible regional variations, though a clear pattern was not immediately evident.YouTube, owned by Google, has expanded its creator tools significantly in recent years to support the platform's more than 2.5 billion monthly users and millions of active channels.

A few shared screenshots showing missing analytics or error screens, urging YouTube to improve communication during technical difficulties.For those unable to access Studio, alternative methods include using third-party analytics tools (where compliant with YouTube's terms) or waiting for mobile app updates.

YouTube periodically rolls out updates to the Studio app that can temporarily introduce or resolve bugs.Looking ahead, industry analysts expect continued enhancements to creator tools, including deeper AI integration for content optimization and monetization insights.
Common issues included subscriber numbers showing as a dash or zero, analytics pages not updating, and generic "something went wrong" prompts when navigating between sections.
On March 10, the platform experienced a widespread partial outage that prevented many creators from accessing their dashboards, triggering panic among some who feared channel termination notices.
YouTube later confirmed the issue was fixed, restoring normal access and accurate statistics.
YouTube's massive scale — processing billions of hours of video daily — makes maintaining 100% uptime a complex engineering challenge.Creators offered mixed reactions online.

While the main YouTube platform for viewers appeared largely unaffected, the creator tools that allow uploading, editing metadata, checking performance and managing channels experienced intermittent disruptions.Downdetector and other outage-tracking sites showed a modest uptick in reports for YouTube-related problems, though not at the scale of major past outages.

However, when core backend services are involved, these steps offer only limited relief.YouTube has invested heavily in creator support infrastructure, including the YouTube Partner Program, dedicated help centers and community forums.
Some expressed frustration at recurring glitches, while others noted that such issues have become somewhat routine and usually resolve quickly.

While not rising to the level of major past outages, the reports highlight ongoing challenges in delivering reliable tools to a global creator base that depends on them for livelihood and audience engagement.As the day progressed, some users noted gradual improvement, with analytics beginning to load or subscriber counts reappearing.

Any disruption draws swift attention because it directly impacts income for those monetizing through ads, memberships, Super Chats and merchandise.Industry observers note that YouTube's rapid feature rollout and heavy reliance on machine learning systems can occasionally lead to backend strain.

Even short disruptions can cascade into lost opportunities, particularly for live streamers or those timing content releases around trending topics.As of Monday afternoon, no widespread confirmation of a full outage had emerged from YouTube.

extraction.body: YouTube has unveiled a host of new features for its content creation platform, YouTube Studio. The updates are aimed at making the creative journey easier and more efficient for creators. The new tools include Ask Studio, an AI-powered feature that provides quick insights on video performance and community feedback. It also includes an Inspiration tab to spark creativity with suggested topics, title testing for optimizing video titles and thumbnails, and advanced auto dubbing, among other features. The Ask Studio feature is designed to answer creators' most pressing questions about their content. It can provide insights into analytics, community engagement, and offer new ideas for future videos. The Inspiration tab, on the other hand, helps creators brainstorm by suggesting topics based on audience behavior. The latest update also includes a feature for creators to collaborate on videos. Up to five collaborators can be added to one video, which will be shown to all participating creators' audiences. Additionally, YouTube is improving its auto-dubbing capabilities with new lip sync technology for translated videos across 20 languages. YouTube is also expanding its likeness detection tool to all creators in the YouTube Partner Program. This technology enables creators to detect, manage, and request the removal of unauthorized videos using their facial likeness. The move is part of YouTube's commitment to building AI technology that responsibly empowers human creativity while protecting creators and their businesses from potential misuse or misrepresentation.

Soon, the company said, users will be able to test up to three video cuts to see which opening hook works best.
Later this year, YouTube Studio will also automatically monitor thumbnail performance and change one proactively if it doesn’t perform well.

At its Made On YouTube annual event, YouTube announced new tools for YouTube Studio, the app creators use to manage their channels, aimed at helping them analyze their videos and grow their audiences.
The updates include expanding Ask Studio, its AI-powered Q&A feature, to iOS and Android, as well as new features that provide feedback on drafts and create dynamic thumbnails.
Creators can also use a new dynamic thumbnail feature to generate three options and show each one to a different segment of their audience.
YouTube also said it’s updating its analytics to go beyond raw numbers, explaining why videos perform the way they do and providing advice about how to make content more engaging.
YouTube is making Shorts more interactive with Google DeepMind’s Veo 3 Fast.
Creators can now generate backgrounds or short clips with sound at no cost.
Most of the new features announced at the Made on YouTube 2025 event will roll out through the rest of 2025 and into early 2026.
He also revealed that YouTube has paid out over $100 billion to creators, artists, and media companies worldwide in the past four years.
Live streaming remains a key driver of interaction, with more than 30% of logged-in YouTube viewers watching live daily in Q2 2025.

AI will assist with automatic product tagging, making it easier for creators to integrate shopping features into their content.

YouTube Studio is evolving into a broader creative hub.

extraction.body: YouTube has unveiled a host of new features for its content creation platform, YouTube Studio. The updates are aimed at making the creative journey easier and more efficient for creators. The new tools include Ask Studio, an AI-powered feature that provides quick insights on video performance and community feedback. It also includes an Inspiration tab to spark creativity with suggested topics, title testing for optimizing video titles and thumbnails, and advanced auto dubbing, among other features. The Ask Studio feature is designed to answer creators' most pressing questions about their content. It can provide insights into analytics, community engagement, and offer new ideas for future videos. The Inspiration tab, on the other hand, helps creators brainstorm by suggesting topics based on audience behavior. The latest update also includes a feature for creators to collaborate on videos. Up to five collaborators can be added to one video, which will be shown to all participating creators' audiences. Additionally, YouTube is improving its auto-dubbing capabilities with new lip sync technology for translated videos across 20 languages. YouTube is also expanding its likeness detection tool to all creators in the YouTube Partner Program. This technology enables creators to detect, manage, and request the removal of unauthorized videos using their facial likeness. The move is part of YouTube's commitment to building AI technology that responsibly empowers human creativity while protecting creators and their businesses from potential misuse or misrepresentation.

passages: Faraday Future expands its EAI Robotics portfolio with nine priced, shipment-ready devices and reports 552 units shipped at a 30% Q2 margin.

LOS ANGELES --(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI ) (“Faraday Future”, “FF” or the “Company”), a California -based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today shared a weekly business update from YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF.
We are bringing 12 years of AI technology and industry capabilities from FF’s automotive business into EAI Robotics.
This foundation has helped us build our Four-Core Full-Stack AI Ecosystem and create a self-evolving flywheel across its four cores.
Within the EAI Devices Core, the full FF EAI Robot World 2.0 lineup is now complete.
It will cover future generations of the nine EAI Devices being unveiled today.
Our goal is to give customers the lowest possible price while delivering much more than the device itself.
Our value formula is simple: “Lowest Price + Four-Core Value + Ongoing Service.”
We are launching nine new EAI Devices across five models, three product series, and two major robot forms.
With this lineup, FF becomes the U.S . robotics company with the widest range of EAI Device forms, the broadest size coverage, and the largest number of product models.
The FF Master Mini—the all-rounder built to go from classroom to competition—comes in three configurations, with prices starting at $9,990 .
The starting price includes a Skills Package valued at $1,000 .
It is the first compact EAI humanoid robot in North America priced below $10,000 to bring education, development, and robotics competition together in one platform.
We have also developed a business model that we call “Light on Four, Heavy on Four.” We stay light on capital, assets, marketing, and sales.
On September 23, FF will hold an EAI Robotics launch event in the Middle East with local partners.
We will launch four EAI Robotics solutions for four key application areas: K–12 education, research, security, and inspection.
Our Education Ecosystem Solutions 1.0 is now officially complete.
Next, let’s turn to the Industry Productivity Solutions Core of FF EAI Robotics.
The most important advantage of our Solutions Core is its ability to turn a one-time robotics project into a standardized productivity asset that can be deployed again and again.

LOS ANGELES --(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI ) (“Faraday Future”, “FF” or the “Company”), a California -based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today shared a weekly business update from YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF. Faraday Future Founder and Global CEO YT Jia Weekly Investor Update: Shares Details from FF’s 919 FF EAI Robotics “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” Ecosystem New Product Series Launch; Four Industry Productivity Solutions, Nine New EAI Devices Unveiled “Hello from weekly report issue No. 73, our special edition for the 919 FF EAI Robotics “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” Ecosystem New Product Series Launch. Hello to all our users, customers, investors, and Futurists around the world! Welcome to our annual 919 event! Take a look. This is what we are building: the world’s one-of-a-kind “One-Brain Multi-Form Multi-Capability” FF EAI Robot World 2.0. Pretty incredible, right? How has FF, in less than a year, built a “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” EAI Robotics Ecosystem that is already gaining a competitive edge? And how have we completed Robot World 2.0 with 24 EAI Devices within the EAI Devices Core? I think there are five key reasons. The first is our forward-looking strategy and our business model. Back in February, we introduced what we believe will be a major direction for the robotics industry: “One Brain, Multiple Forms; Multiple Forms, Multiple Capabilities.” Some of our industry peers, including Figure, are following a “One Form Does It All” approach. We respect their work, but we believe this approach has clear limits and will not be the best long-term path for robotics. Dr. Fei-Fei Li recently shared a similar view that different robot forms will coexist. We have also developed a business model that we call “Light on Four, Heavy on Four.” We stay light on capital, assets, marketing, and sales. At the same time, we put our greatest focus on product power, AI, real-world utility, and our users. This helps us move from strategy to execution much faster. And the results are starting to show. As of the end of August, cumulative shipments and sales of FF EAI robots reached 552 units. In the Q2 financial results we released, the average contribution margin on our robotics products was approximately 30% . These results are also a strong sign that users recognize the real-world value of our Four-Core Full-Stack AI robots. The second reason is how we develop our products and technology: through in-house development plus open collaboration. We are bringing 12 years of AI technology and industry capabilities from FF’s automotive business into EAI Robotics. This foundation has helped us build our Four-Core Full-Stack AI Ecosystem and create a self-evolving flywheel across its four cores. Within the EAI Devices Core, the full FF EAI Robot World 2.0 lineup is now complete. Our “Built in USA” program is also moving forward according to its three-phase timeline. It will cover future generations of the nine EAI Devices being unveiled today. The third reason is our work in supply chain, manufacturing, and compliance. Through the “Built in USA” Acceleration Program, we are bringing the capabilities and resources developed over many years in the EAI EV industry into EAI Robotics. This helps us turn our existing strengths into competitive advantages much faster. The fourth reason is our user ecosystem. We give customers three ways to access our products: the EAI Device, the EAI Device + Skills, and the EAI Device + Industry Solutions. Together with our “6+1” Direct Sales and Robot-Sharing Rental Network, these offerings allow us to serve both B2B and B2C markets and continue supporting customers after delivery. A one-time product sale can grow into a long-term customer relationship and a continuing source of ecosystem revenue. And the fifth reason is the industry alliance we are building. Through our Global EAI Industry Bridge and the EAI Robotics “Made in USA” Alliance, we are bringing more suppliers, customers, and capital partners into our ecosystem. Today’s event will focus on new products from two of our four cores: the EAI Devices Core and the Industry Productivity Solutions Core. Let me give you a quick preview. There are five things to watch today. First, EAI Devices. We are launching nine new EAI Devices across five models, three product series, and two major robot forms. They will go on sale today and be available for immediate delivery. With this lineup, FF becomes the U.S . robotics company with the widest range of EAI Device forms, the broadest size coverage, and the largest number of product models. For industries and users, this means an EAI Brain, solutions, and data, all covering the widest range of device forms. Second, Industry Productivity Solutions. We will launch four EAI Robotics solutions for four key application areas: K–12 education, research, security, and inspection. extraction.body: XRP Leads Crypto Losses as Ethereum, Dogecoin Prices Crater Alongside Bitcoin XRP was the worst-performing altcoin among the leading cryptocurrencies Thursday morning, showing a 15% drop over the last 24 hours as markets swing bearish and Bitcoin extends its losses . At the time of writing, XRP was trading for $1.30 after having dropped roughly 28% in the past week, according to crypto price aggregator CoinGecko. An earlier dip to $1.28 marked the lowest price for the Ripple-linked asset since November 2024, when XRP surged in the wake of President Trump's election win. It's also the biggest daily drop of any coin in the top 100 cryptocurrencies by market cap over the last day. Ethereum was recently trading at $1,985 after plunging 6% on the day and losing about 30% of its value in the last week, while original meme coin Dogecoin is down about 8% on the day to $0.09, shedding nearly 19% of its value over the past seven days. BNB was recently changing hands for $666 after having dropped 9% in the past day, losing 23% in the past seven days. Solana had dipped to $85, after falling about 8% in the past day, and was 27% lower than it was this time last week. Bitcoin dove below the $67,000 mark Thursday morning, but was recently trading just above $68,000. The drawdown has resulted in the liquidiation of more than $47 million worth of XRP derivatives contracts. extraction.body: XRP Leads Crypto Losses as Ethereum, Dogecoin Prices Crater Alongside Bitcoin XRP was the worst-performing altcoin among the leading cryptocurrencies Thursday morning, showing a 15% drop over the last 24 hours as markets swing bearish and Bitcoin extends its losses . At the time of writing, XRP was trading for $1.30 after having dropped roughly 28% in the past week, according to crypto price aggregator CoinGecko. An earlier dip to $1.28 marked the lowest price for the Ripple-linked asset since November 2024, when XRP surged in the wake of President Trump's election win. It's also the biggest daily drop of any coin in the top 100 cryptocurrencies by market cap over the last day. Ethereum was recently trading at $1,985 after plunging 6% on the day and losing about 30% of its value in the last week, while original meme coin Dogecoin is down about 8% on the day to $0.09, shedding nearly 19% of its value over the past seven days. BNB was recently changing hands for $666 after having dropped 9% in the past day, losing 23% in the past seven days. Solana had dipped to $85, after falling about 8% in the past day, and was 27% lower than it was this time last week. Bitcoin dove below the $67,000 mark Thursday morning, but was recently trading just above $68,000. The drawdown has resulted in the liquidiation of more than $47 million worth of XRP derivatives contracts. And the bulk of them, nearly $44 million worth, were long on XRP, according to on-chain analytics platform CoinGlass. Overall, more than $1.43 billion worth of crypto positions have been liquidated in the last day. The platform also shows that XRP trading volume has jumped by 57%, with over $11 billion worth of coins changing hands in the past 24 hours. The global crypto market capitalization has now fallen 7.4% on the day to $2.37 trillion after having peaked above $4.2 trillion in September 2025. Meanwhile, XRP treasury firm Evernorth now has a $446 million unrealized loss on its 388,710,631 XRP stash. The company debuted as an XRP treasury in October, saying that its goal was to raise more than $1 billion to buy XRP. It also has backing from Ripple, whose executives are acting as strategic advisors to the firm. In late October, the company spent $947 million buying XRP. It hasn't made another buy since then, but it has watched the value of its XRP holdings drop sharply to approximately $501 million. The company didn't immediately respond to a request for comment from Decrypt . XRP ETF inflows slowed down, but didn't turn red yesterday. The seven spot XRP ETFs that are trading in the U.S. saw $5.9 million in volume and net inflows of $6.9 million on Wednesday, according to an ETF tracker maintained by XRP Insights. Ripple Labs CEO Brad Garlinghouse has been outspoken about the "absolute firestorm of action to get the Market Structure bill passed," but hasn't commented on markets going bearish. Crypto traders are broadly feeling skittish about current market conditions. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index maintained by CoinGlass has dropped to 11, firmly in the "Extreme Fear" category. During the month of January, it very briefly ticked into the greed category when the index peaked at 62, but has been steadily declining since then. Bitcoin has shot from $60,000 to $85,000 in just two weeks.

Cardano has chosen a different route than the path followed by Ethereum and Solana.
Cardano is a research-focused blockchain led by a highly technical team that prioritizes compliance and technological accuracy over speed and marketing.
This is evident in Cardano’s 100% uptime and interest expressed by governments and academic institutions.
There’s no one “best” crypto for a $1,000 investment.
Conservative investors consider Bitcoin or Ethereum as core long‑term holdings, while growth-oriented investors prefer smaller‑cap tokens for their upside potential despite the higher risk.
Ethereum is mid-cycle in a meaningful upgrade sequence.
Pectra (live since May 2026) already increased validator staking limits and improved wallet UX.

ETH staking yields currently sit around 3–4% annually, which adds a carry component most blue chips can’t offer.
BNB’s investment case rests on two things: Binance’s continued market share dominance (still the largest CEX by volume), and BNB Chain’s growing ecosystem beyond the exchange.

If you use DeFi often, that combination can make BNB more practical to hold and use.

Meme coins like Dogecoin and Pepe also rank among the most actively traded tokens.

sources.title: Gov. JB Pritzker assembling Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet to assess AI threats - Chicago Sun-Times
passages: The Democratic governor signed an executive order Tuesday establishing the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet to assess “the various risks posed by Al to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.”

JB Pritzker is convening a panel of experts to advise state officials on the potential threats of artificial intelligence as a growing number of industry leaders warn the burgeoning, self-improving technology could spell doomsday for humanity if left unchecked.

Pritzker will name his AI Cabinet members “in the coming weeks” to work alongside numerous state agency leaders, including from the Department of Innovation and Technology, the Department of Public Health and the Illinois Emergency Management Agency.
“Illinois has already enacted nation-leading laws that hold Big Tech accountable and today I’m taking executive action to keep this a priority,” Pritzker said.

They’re expected to come from backgrounds in academia, law, ethics and governance, and provide recommendations on potential public safety threats, protecting public assets and evaluating possible regulations, according to Pritzker’s office.
From WBUR and NPR, co-hosted by Robin Young and Scott Tong, with news from Chicago from WBEZ’s Lisa Labuz.

JB Pritzker is convening a panel of experts to advise state officials on the potential threats of artificial intelligence as a growing number of industry leaders warn the burgeoning, self-improving technology could spell doomsday for humanity if left unchecked. The Democratic governor signed an executive order Tuesday establishing the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet to assess “the various risks posed by Al to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.” Pritzker will name his AI Cabinet members “in the coming weeks” to work alongside numerous state agency leaders, including from the Department of Innovation and Technology, the Department of Public Health and the Illinois Emergency Management Agency. Pritzker, who has done little to quell speculation about his own presidential ambitions, has blasted President Donald Trump for his administration’s lax approach to AI regulation. “Illinois has already enacted nation-leading laws that hold Big Tech accountable and today I’m taking executive action to keep this a priority,” Pritzker said. “Congress and the White House need to treat AI risks with urgency, but in the meantime, Illinois won’t wait because it is our foremost responsibility to prepare and protect Illinoisans.” University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign Chancellor Charles Isbell said in a statement that his institution is “eager to help the state navigate the current challenges and opportunities that AI brings.” “As a land-grant institution, we are committed to innovation for the public good and to developing human-centered AI that protects privacy, reduces bias, strengthens democratic institutions, uses energy wisely, and creates value for workers, companies and communities,” Isbell said.

extraction.body: SPRINGFIELD — Gov. JB Pritzker is setting up a new group within state government to explore more regulations for artificial intelligence as calls grow across the country for new restrictions. Pritzker signed an executive order on Tuesday to establish an AI Cabinet made up of experts and representatives from several state agencies. The unpaid group, which will formulate policy proposals through 2027, will analyze and assess “the various risks posed by AI to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.” It’s the latest move by Illinois to tackle state-focused AI regulation as the federal government continues to take a hands-off approach , even as industry insiders sound the alarm on the technology’s capabilities. A former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher alleged in an explosive social media post earlier this month that AI companies are building a tool that could become “out of control” and pose a threat to human existence by 2030. “Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” Pritzker said in a statement. The cabinet will formulate policies and procedures to protect Illinois residents and public assets like water systems, education and information systems from threats posed by AI. It will also analyze “emerging AI incidents and share lessons learned” from them. The advisory group will also make policy recommendations on risk management and assess the feasibility, timeframe and any other challenges for implementing them. The cabinet will consider regulations tying data center incentives or operational approval to a company’s ability to meet safety, accountability and transparency standards. It will also look into addressing strain on the energy grid from data centers, evaluating how state procurement and contracting practices can incorporate AI safety and accountability measures, and assessing if existing legal options are good enough to hold AI companies that cause harm accountable. Illinois lawmakers have already taken steps to regulate AI. Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315 in July, also known as the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act , which increases transparency and accountability requirements for the largest artificial intelligence models — those that generate more than $500 million in annual revenue and are trained using massive computing power. It establishes new reporting standards for the possibility that the AI model could be used for large-scale harm, such as by helping create a chemical, biological or nuclear weapon or committing cyber-attacks. It also made Illinois the first state to require annual audits of AI. The law takes effect in 2028. Since the whistleblower came forward earlier this month, Pritzker has been aggressively calling on Congress to step in. “It should be among the top priorities, but don't misunderstand, it is dangerous and it's dangerous on the level of nuclear weapons,” Pritzker said on ABC’s Sunday morning news show . “So that's why it needs to be an international endeavor. Pritzker has urged Congress to immediately begin holding hearings on AI safety and impose national standards. The cabinet will formulate policies and procedures to protect Illinois residents and public assets like water systems, education and information systems from threats posed by AI. It will also analyze “emerging AI incidents and share lessons learned” from them.
The advisory group will also make policy recommendations on risk management and assess the feasibility, timeframe and any other challenges for implementing them.

The cabinet will consider regulations tying data center incentives or operational approval to a company’s ability to meet safety, accountability and transparency standards. It will also look into addressing strain on the energy grid from data centers, evaluating how state procurement and contracting practices can incorporate AI safety and accountability measures, and assessing if existing legal options are good enough to hold AI companies that cause harm accountable.
Illinois lawmakers have already taken steps to regulate AI.

Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315 in July, also known as the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act , which increases transparency and accountability requirements for the largest artificial intelligence models — those that generate more than $500 million in annual revenue and are trained using massive computing power. It establishes new reporting standards for the possibility that the AI model could be used for large-scale harm, such as by helping create a chemical, biological or nuclear weapon or committing cyber-attacks.
It also made Illinois the first state to require annual audits of AI. The law takes effect in 2028.
Since the whistleblower came forward earlier this month, Pritzker has been aggressively calling on Congress to step in.

“It should be among the top priorities, but don't misunderstand, it is dangerous and it's dangerous on the level of nuclear weapons,” Pritzker said on ABC’s Sunday morning news show . “So that's why it needs to be an international endeavor.
Pritzker has urged Congress to immediately begin holding hearings on AI safety and impose national standards.

sources.title: OpenAI’s Altman and Anthropic’s Amodei address UN security council - The Guardian
passages: Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic, heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies, addressed the United Nations security council on Wednesday in separate briefings on AI safety.
Altman and Amodei spoke as their companies face increasing scrutiny over the safety of their products.
Public alarm over AI has grown in response to warnings from Anthropic researchers earlier this month that the technology could destroy humanity within the decade.
He advocated for governments to come together to build a future where AI is guided by democratic institutions, rather than one where people feel like the technology is “something being done to them”.
Earlier, Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development, which was supported by OpenAI , Google and Elon Musk.

Altman argued there was instead a “middle path” through the safety debate that should be based on three principles: AI systems must remain under human control; AI must benefit people, from helping doctors treat patients to boosting entrepreneurs; and the technology must “empower people individually”.

While Altman steered his address away from engaging with the warnings of existential risk that have made headlines this month, Amodei reiterated his concerns about developers losing control of AI while also framing his company as an industry leader on safety.
“If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” Amodei said.
“At Anthropic, we believe we have the best track record in the industry for preventing these risks”.
Their companies are also jockeying for the lead in the AI race, with both eyeing potentially record-setting initial public offerings that would value each at more than $1.5tn.
“We have a choice in front of us,” Altman told the council.
“AI can either be more like a new renaissance of creativity and discovery, or more like a new industrial revolution of upheaval and disarray.”
“If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone.
They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people that they serve,” Altman said.

Public alarm over AI has grown in response to warnings from Anthropic researchers earlier this month that the technology could destroy humanity within the decade. Leaders of AI companies, including Altman and Amodei, have since called for a slowdown on advancing AI and more international cooperation on the technology’s safety standards. Altman, who sat at the corner of the security council’s horseshoe-shaped table and spoke for about 10 minutes, touted AI’s benefits to productivity while also warning of its potential abuses. He advocated for governments to come together to build a future where AI is guided by democratic institutions, rather than one where people feel like the technology is “something being done to them”. “If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people that they serve,” Altman said. The OpenAI CEO’s speech contrasted with some of his company’s lobbying efforts and the political action committee of its president, Greg Brockman. The pro-AI Leading the Future PAC has accrued more than $100m and spent millions targeting candidates who support stronger regulation on the AI industry. Altman’s speech also nodded to some of the concerns from Anthropic researchers about AI’s existential risk, warning the council against falling into “doomerism”. Altman argued there was instead a “middle path” through the safety debate that should be based on three principles: AI systems must remain under human control; AI must benefit people, from helping doctors treat patients to boosting entrepreneurs; and the technology must “empower people individually”. Amodei, who addressed the council via video call, repeated many of the points that he made in a 12 September blog post that called for increased global cooperation and oversight of AI. He advocated for several forms of international agreements, including a ban on using AI to develop biological weapons and global standards for testing new AI models. While Altman steered his address away from engaging with the warnings of existential risk that have made headlines this month, Amodei reiterated his concerns about developers losing control of AI while also framing his company as an industry leader on safety. “If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” Amodei said. “At Anthropic, we believe we have the best track record in the industry for preventing these risks”. AI regulation has shot up the political agenda after researchers at OpenAI’s arch-rival Anthropic warned the technology could wipe out humanity within years. These concerns are a regular refrain within sections of the AI community, who fear the technology could trigger devastation for a variety of reasons ranging from aiding development of bioweapons to triggering a financial catastrophe. Earlier, Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development, which was supported by OpenAI , Google and Elon Musk. Both Amodei and Altman have long cast themselves as stewards of AI and sought to shape how the technology is publicly received. Their companies are also jockeying for the lead in the AI race, with both eyeing potentially record-setting initial public offerings that would value each at more than $1.5tn.

coreStoryFacts.text: Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic, heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies, addressed the United Nations security council on Wednesday in separate briefings on AI safety.
Altman and Amodei spoke as their companies face increasing scrutiny over the safety of their products.
Public alarm over AI has grown in response to warnings from Anthropic researchers earlier this month that the technology could destroy humanity within the decade.
He advocated for governments to come together to build a future where AI is guided by democratic institutions, rather than one where people feel like the technology is “something being done to them”.
Earlier, Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development, which was supported by OpenAI , Google and Elon Musk.

Altman argued there was instead a “middle path” through the safety debate that should be based on three principles: AI systems must remain under human control; AI must benefit people, from helping doctors treat patients to boosting entrepreneurs; and the technology must “empower people individually”.

While Altman steered his address away from engaging with the warnings of existential risk that have made headlines this month, Amodei reiterated his concerns about developers losing control of AI while also framing his company as an industry leader on safety.
“If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” Amodei said.
“At Anthropic, we believe we have the best track record in the industry for preventing these risks”.
Their companies are also jockeying for the lead in the AI race, with both eyeing potentially record-setting initial public offerings that would value each at more than $1.5tn.
“We have a choice in front of us,” Altman told the council.
“AI can either be more like a new renaissance of creativity and discovery, or more like a new industrial revolution of upheaval and disarray.”
“If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone.
They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people that they serve,” Altman said.

extraction.body: Heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies give separate briefings on AI safety Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic, heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies, addressed the United Nations security council on Wednesday in separate briefings on AI safety. “We have a choice in front of us,” Altman told the council. “AI can either be more like a new renaissance of creativity and discovery, or more like a new industrial revolution of upheaval and disarray.” Altman and Amodei spoke as their companies face increasing scrutiny over the safety of their products. Public alarm over AI has grown in response to warnings from Anthropic researchers earlier this month that the technology could destroy humanity within the decade. Leaders of AI companies, including Altman and Amodei, have since called for a slowdown on advancing AI and more international cooperation on the technology’s safety standards. Altman, who sat at the corner of the security council’s horseshoe-shaped table and spoke for about 10 minutes, touted AI’s benefits to productivity while also warning of its potential abuses. He advocated for governments to come together to build a future where AI is guided by democratic institutions, rather than one where people feel like the technology is “something being done to them”. “If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people that they serve,” Altman said. The OpenAI CEO’s speech contrasted with some of his company’s lobbying efforts and the political action committee of its president, Greg Brockman. The pro-AI Leading the Future PAC has accrued more than $100m and spent millions targeting candidates who support stronger regulation on the AI industry. Altman’s speech also nodded to some of the concerns from Anthropic researchers about AI’s existential risk, warning the council against falling into “doomerism”. Altman argued there was instead a “middle path” through the safety debate that should be based on three principles: AI systems must remain under human control; AI must benefit people, from helping doctors treat patients to boosting entrepreneurs; and the technology must “empower people individually”. Amodei, who addressed the council via video call, repeated many of the points that he made in a 12 September blog post that called for increased global cooperation and oversight of AI. He advocated for several forms of international agreements, including a ban on using AI to develop biological weapons and global standards for testing new AI models. While Altman steered his address away from engaging with the warnings of existential risk that have made headlines this month, Amodei reiterated his concerns about developers losing control of AI while also framing his company as an industry leader on safety. “If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” Amodei said. “At Anthropic, we believe we have the best track record in the industry for preventing these risks”. AI regulation has shot up the political agenda after researchers at OpenAI’s arch-rival Anthropic warned the technology could wipe out humanity within years. These concerns are a regular refrain within sections of the AI community, who fear the technology could trigger devastation for a variety of reasons ranging from aiding development of bioweapons to triggering a financial catastrophe. Earlier, Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development, which was supported by OpenAI , Google and Elon Musk. Both Amodei and Altman have long cast themselves as stewards of AI and sought to shape how the technology is publicly received. Their companies are also jockeying for the lead in the AI race, with both eyeing potentially record-setting initial public offerings that would value each at more than $1.5tn.

Altman and Amodei spoke as their companies face increasing scrutiny over the safety of their products. Public alarm over AI has grown in response to warnings from Anthropic researchers earlier this month that the technology could destroy humanity within the decade. Leaders of AI companies, including Altman and Amodei, have since called for a slowdown on advancing AI and more international cooperation on the technology’s safety standards.

Altman, who sat at the corner of the security council’s horseshoe-shaped table and spoke for about 10 minutes, touted AI’s benefits to productivity while also warning of its potential abuses. He advocated for governments to come together to build a future where AI is guided by democratic institutions, rather than one where people feel like the technology is “something being done to them”.

“If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people that they serve,” Altman said.

The pro-AI Leading the Future PAC has accrued more than $100m and spent millions targeting candidates who support stronger regulation on the AI industry.

He advocated for several forms of international agreements, including a ban on using AI to develop biological weapons and global standards for testing new AI models.

While Altman steered his address away from engaging with the warnings of existential risk that have made headlines this month, Amodei reiterated his concerns about developers losing control of AI while also framing his company as an industry leader on safety.

extraction.body: President Donald Trump's White House media ban is backfiring to the point where he may begin to question his entire existence. On The Daily Beast Podcast , political expert David Rothkopf previewed what may be in store for the president after he initiated a constitutionally questionable White House ban on CNN, Politico, and MS NOW because he didn't like their coverage. On Monday, the consequences of that move were seen when NBC, ABC, CBS, and Fox News, along with photographers from major wire agencies and news outlets, united to pause White House television pool coverage, leaving Trump inaudible—even on the White House's own livestream . Since the 80-year-old president loves being on television, Rothkopf said, this could spark an internal crisis. "I think if Trump stopped being covered—if this media blackout, this boycott kicked in—he would start wondering about his own existence," Rothkopf told host Joanna Coles. "I think he doesn't believe he exists unless he reads or sees about himself on TV." "He wants to be the center of attention. All he wants in life is to be on TV. It's his obsession," Rothkopf continued. "How long before Trump folds on all of this? Because [the networks] didn't say they're not providing coverage today; they said they're not providing coverage indefinitely, and there is no plan for replacement coverage." Trump is scheduled to speak this week at the United Nations General Assembly in New York, and to host Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House. When he spoke Monday at the new South Lawn helipad, which he wanted finished in time for Xi's visit, he was inaudible. "Do you think there will be internal fury at Natalie Harp for not seeing around the corner of what banning MS NOW and CNN would actually do?" Coles asked. "I don't think the response from the professionals, such as they are in the White House, is going to be good. Notably from Susie Wiles, particularly if she reads the Daily Beast piece on the background on this, on Natalie Harp," he said. "And as we know, the White House reads the Daily Beast all the time. They're obsessed with the Daily Beast, possibly because of Natalie Harp... You can just imagine late at night, Natalie Harp is there saying, 'I am your only true follower. I'm the only one who loves you. Here is some nice AI slop pictures of you with your shirt off. You look very attractive. And these mean people out there coming to get you.'" "And they're in the bubble, the Natalie-Don bubble, of how he wants to be perceived, how he wants to be loved. And she just plays to all of his worst impulses," Rothkopf said. Meanwhile, Wiles has probably been hearing from Republicans in Congress concerned about how this is playing out when the midterms are looming, he continued. "I saw a story this morning... that was talking about how Republicans are starting to say, 'Well, Trump is toxic because his approval ratings are down in the 30s.' They're falling. On some issues, they're in the 20s. This is bad, bad news coming up to an election, and Susie Wiles is the shock absorber who gets those calls," he said, as a new poll on Monday showed the president sinking to just 29 percent approval. "So I'm sure she is super unhappy with this. I can't imagine she and Natalie are besties," Rothkopf said. "But frankly, the other sycophants in the White House all want to be up in Trump's drawers like Natalie. I think they're jealous. You know, I think everybody's jealous of the fact that this 35-year-old woman has found the inside track to the president by playing to his absolute obsession with how he is covered in the media." Banning the three networks was also a "bad idea" Rothkopf said, because it didn't turn out well when the Trump administration revoked then-CNN correspondent Jim Acosta's press pass. "The last term he did it to Jim Acosta of CNN, who went to court and got his pass reinstated because, you know, there is the First Amendment still. But nonetheless, Trump has done this. And it finally moved one of the slowest-responding, most pusillanimous organizations in Washington to action—which is to say White House correspondents—because they have watched week in and week out as he has abused women, particularly Kaitlan Collins of CNN and others, and they haven't done anything. But finally this was a straw too much." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. passages: The newly minted MAGA-approved TV pool appears to have inadvertently made itself a security risk for the president.

With Trump’s ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, the other networks responsible for TV pool duty—ABC, CBS, NBC, and Fox—have said they will stand in solidarity with their media colleagues and not honor their scheduled pool coverage.
The same day the major networks announced they were standing with CNN in solidarity, the White House tried to fight back by launching what it called “TRUMP TV,” which airs round the clock.

extraction.body: The newly minted MAGA-approved TV pool appears to have inadvertently made itself a security risk for the president. The pro-Trump outlet Real America’s Voice became the primary television crew traveling with President Donald Trump to the United Nations General Assembly this week after he banned CNN, which was scheduled to provide a pool feed from New York on Monday, from the White House. Real America’s Voice, now tasked with providing footage to media partners, shared footage from inside Trump’s motorcade as he was driven off of the UN campus and out of New York. The video was hailed by online MAGA flacks, including Nick Sortor, who said he was grateful to Real America’s Voice for “showing us RAW footage of how difficult it is to keep President Trump safe.” In reality, they may have breached an all-important protocol. Former White House Correspondents’ Association President Weijia Jiang of CBS News poured cold water on the apparent access the public was getting. “For decades, the [WHCA] has advised poolers not to air video of taillights because it’s a potential risk to the security of the motorcade,” she said. Several big-name journalists endorsed her post, including ABC’s Jonathan Karl, CNN’s Brian Stelter, and Face the Nation host Margaret Breman, among others. Former WHCA President Kelly O’Donnell of NBC News echoed the sentiment, posting that the association has “long provided specific guidance from the Secret Service and various administrations on matters where video material should not be used at all or with limitations for security reasons.” Each presidential motorcade features at least two identical Cadillac limousines, each displaying the presidential seal and American flags, which is intended to make it impossible for the average spectator to know which vehicle is carrying the president. Their footage from inside the motorcade shows the New York Police Department escorting the presidential motorcade out of the UN campus and onto a New York City highway. With Trump’s ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, the other networks responsible for TV pool duty—ABC, CBS, NBC, and Fox—have said they will stand in solidarity with their media colleagues and not honor their scheduled pool coverage. That means pool coverage has fallen to MAGA media outlets like Real America’s Voice and Lindell TV, which is owned by the 2020 election denier Mike Lindell. Performance One Media, a Colorado-based media company run by Robert Sigg, owns Real America’s Voice. Sigg appears to be a more unsavory character, as he has gotten in trouble with the law for domestic violence, burglary, drug distribution, driving under the influence, and assault, charges that were later dropped. He also has a white-collar crime track record, having pleaded guilty to one count of bank fraud stemming from his role in a $19 million mortgage-fraud scheme. In 2013, his son, Austin, was sentenced to life in prison at age 17 in 2013 for kidnapping and murdering 10-year-old Jessica Ridgeway. Sigg’s outlet is best-known for airing Steve Bannon’s War Room show. The same day the major networks announced they were standing with CNN in solidarity, the White House tried to fight back by launching what it called “TRUMP TV,” which airs round the clock. It has tried to sell the programming as giving people the ability to “watch the Trump Administration’s biggest moments all in one place.” But there appears to be little interest in the new venture, as live viewership has been as low as 500 people on YouTube.

extraction.body: President Donald Trump's White House media ban is backfiring to the point where he may begin to question his entire existence. On The Daily Beast Podcast , political expert David Rothkopf previewed what may be in store for the president after he initiated a constitutionally questionable White House ban on CNN, Politico, and MS NOW because he didn't like their coverage. On Monday, the consequences of that move were seen when NBC, ABC, CBS, and Fox News, along with photographers from major wire agencies and news outlets, united to pause White House television pool coverage, leaving Trump inaudible—even on the White House's own livestream . Since the 80-year-old president loves being on television, Rothkopf said, this could spark an internal crisis. "I think if Trump stopped being covered—if this media blackout, this boycott kicked in—he would start wondering about his own existence," Rothkopf told host Joanna Coles. "I think he doesn't believe he exists unless he reads or sees about himself on TV." "He wants to be the center of attention. All he wants in life is to be on TV. It's his obsession," Rothkopf continued. "How long before Trump folds on all of this? Because [the networks] didn't say they're not providing coverage today; they said they're not providing coverage indefinitely, and there is no plan for replacement coverage." Trump is scheduled to speak this week at the United Nations General Assembly in New York, and to host Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House. When he spoke Monday at the new South Lawn helipad, which he wanted finished in time for Xi's visit, he was inaudible. "Do you think there will be internal fury at Natalie Harp for not seeing around the corner of what banning MS NOW and CNN would actually do?" Coles asked. "I don't think the response from the professionals, such as they are in the White House, is going to be good. Notably from Susie Wiles, particularly if she reads the Daily Beast piece on the background on this, on Natalie Harp," he said. "And as we know, the White House reads the Daily Beast all the time. They're obsessed with the Daily Beast, possibly because of Natalie Harp... You can just imagine late at night, Natalie Harp is there saying, 'I am your only true follower. I'm the only one who loves you. Here is some nice AI slop pictures of you with your shirt off. You look very attractive. And these mean people out there coming to get you.'" "And they're in the bubble, the Natalie-Don bubble, of how he wants to be perceived, how he wants to be loved. And she just plays to all of his worst impulses," Rothkopf said. Meanwhile, Wiles has probably been hearing from Republicans in Congress concerned about how this is playing out when the midterms are looming, he continued. "I saw a story this morning... that was talking about how Republicans are starting to say, 'Well, Trump is toxic because his approval ratings are down in the 30s.' They're falling. On some issues, they're in the 20s. This is bad, bad news coming up to an election, and Susie Wiles is the shock absorber who gets those calls," he said, as a new poll on Monday showed the president sinking to just 29 percent approval. "So I'm sure she is super unhappy with this. I can't imagine she and Natalie are besties," Rothkopf said. "But frankly, the other sycophants in the White House all want to be up in Trump's drawers like Natalie. I think they're jealous. You know, I think everybody's jealous of the fact that this 35-year-old woman has found the inside track to the president by playing to his absolute obsession with how he is covered in the media." Banning the three networks was also a "bad idea" Rothkopf said, because it didn't turn out well when the Trump administration revoked then-CNN correspondent Jim Acosta's press pass. "The last term he did it to Jim Acosta of CNN, who went to court and got his pass reinstated because, you know, there is the First Amendment still. But nonetheless, Trump has done this. And it finally moved one of the slowest-responding, most pusillanimous organizations in Washington to action—which is to say White House correspondents—because they have watched week in and week out as he has abused women, particularly Kaitlan Collins of CNN and others, and they haven't done anything. But finally this was a straw too much." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. extraction.body: The newly minted MAGA-approved TV pool appears to have inadvertently made itself a security risk for the president. The pro-Trump outlet Real America’s Voice became the primary television crew traveling with President Donald Trump to the United Nations General Assembly this week after he banned CNN, which was scheduled to provide a pool feed from New York on Monday, from the White House. Real America’s Voice, now tasked with providing footage to media partners, shared footage from inside Trump’s motorcade as he was driven off of the UN campus and out of New York. The video was hailed by online MAGA flacks, including Nick Sortor, who said he was grateful to Real America’s Voice for “showing us RAW footage of how difficult it is to keep President Trump safe.” In reality, they may have breached an all-important protocol. Former White House Correspondents’ Association President Weijia Jiang of CBS News poured cold water on the apparent access the public was getting. “For decades, the [WHCA] has advised poolers not to air video of taillights because it’s a potential risk to the security of the motorcade,” she said. Several big-name journalists endorsed her post, including ABC’s Jonathan Karl, CNN’s Brian Stelter, and Face the Nation host Margaret Breman, among others. Former WHCA President Kelly O’Donnell of NBC News echoed the sentiment, posting that the association has “long provided specific guidance from the Secret Service and various administrations on matters where video material should not be used at all or with limitations for security reasons.” Each presidential motorcade features at least two identical Cadillac limousines, each displaying the presidential seal and American flags, which is intended to make it impossible for the average spectator to know which vehicle is carrying the president. Their footage from inside the motorcade shows the New York Police Department escorting the presidential motorcade out of the UN campus and onto a New York City highway. With Trump’s ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, the other networks responsible for TV pool duty—ABC, CBS, NBC, and Fox—have said they will stand in solidarity with their media colleagues and not honor their scheduled pool coverage. That means pool coverage has fallen to MAGA media outlets like Real America’s Voice and Lindell TV, which is owned by the 2020 election denier Mike Lindell. Performance One Media, a Colorado-based media company run by Robert Sigg, owns Real America’s Voice. Sigg appears to be a more unsavory character, as he has gotten in trouble with the law for domestic violence, burglary, drug distribution, driving under the influence, and assault, charges that were later dropped. He also has a white-collar crime track record, having pleaded guilty to one count of bank fraud stemming from his role in a $19 million mortgage-fraud scheme. In 2013, his son, Austin, was sentenced to life in prison at age 17 in 2013 for kidnapping and murdering 10-year-old Jessica Ridgeway. Sigg’s outlet is best-known for airing Steve Bannon’s War Room show. The same day the major networks announced they were standing with CNN in solidarity, the White House tried to fight back by launching what it called “TRUMP TV,” which airs round the clock. It has tried to sell the programming as giving people the ability to “watch the Trump Administration’s biggest moments all in one place.” But there appears to be little interest in the new venture, as live viewership has been as low as 500 people on YouTube.

passages: Meta is renewing its quest to make virtual reality a thing.
At Connect on Wednesday, the company announced Meta VR Glasses, its newest entry into the VR market.
These glasses actually seem quite promising given their substantially lighter form factor and a host of new entertainment integrations — including (allegedly) IMAX compatibility.

sources.title: Meta’s New VR Glasses to Entice Casual Viewers With 3D and Full-Frame IMAX - IGN
passages: In addition to all your streaming favorites (Prime Video, YouTube, DIRECTV, AMC+, Crunchyroll, Plex, and vitally, Tubi), Meta has teamed up with IMAX to bring the world of full-frame, 1:43:1 IMAX movies to your headset.
Currently, this is poised to be the only way to watch something like The Odyssey in its native aspect ratio outside of a handful of cinemas.
Sadly, that option wasn’t available during our limited tech demo, but it sets Meta VR Glasses apart even from Blu-ray and UHD, which only expand to the size of your HD television — a paltry 16:9.

A strange way to begin a marketing pitch, but a surprisingly welcome one, as she echoed thoughts that have likely been on the mind of anyone who has thus far rejected the industry’s clunky VR-sphere, and its closed-off headsets akin to ski goggles.
The Meta Quest (and like it, the Apple Vision Pro) haven’t exactly pivoted society towards Ready Player One, and perhaps we’re better for it.

Tech companies have gradually invaded the film festival space, but Meta’s secret new project was a perfect fit for this year’s Toronto International Film Festival, both because of its entertainment capabilities, and because it feels straight out of a movie.

Not far from where I’d soon watch the new Zack Snyder film , a makeshift gallery played host to covert keynote presentations, each with an audience of one, as a well-dressed entertainment executive showed surprising candor.
The 3D isn’t too bad either (as evidenced by a short clip of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness), though the effect is no more or less immersive than most current 3D television sets.
Upon launch, 3D offerings will be available from the likes of HBO Max, Paramount+ and Peacock.

However, where things get really novel is the switch from movies to sports, where you have the option of not just watching your game of choice with a 180-degree field of view — in this case, Game 4 of the 2026 NBA finals; go Knicks — but sitting in a variety of courtside seats and glancing around.

Then again, between the NBA finals and the FIFA World Cup, if this summer has proved anything, it’s that sports are a social event, so closing yourself off this way might at best be a backup for plans that fall through.
That is, unless Meta plans to roll out highly involved tech demos for every potential buyer.
There’s a candy store feeling to wearing one of these and turning around to see a fully (or semi) rendered space behind you, waiting to be filled.
Much like legs in the Metaverse, it’s coming, baby.

extraction.body: Tech companies have gradually invaded the film festival space, but Meta’s secret new project was a perfect fit for this year’s Toronto International Film Festival, both because of its entertainment capabilities, and because it feels straight out of a movie. Not far from where I’d soon watch the new Zack Snyder film , a makeshift gallery played host to covert keynote presentations, each with an audience of one, as a well-dressed entertainment executive showed surprising candor. “We are… self-aware,” she sighed. A strange way to begin a marketing pitch, but a surprisingly welcome one, as she echoed thoughts that have likely been on the mind of anyone who has thus far rejected the industry’s clunky VR-sphere, and its closed-off headsets akin to ski goggles. The Meta Quest (and like it, the Apple Vision Pro) haven’t exactly pivoted society towards Ready Player One, and perhaps we’re better for it. However, the reveal of Meta’s new entertainment-centric gizmo, Meta VR Glasses, arriving this spring, might just be enough of a departure to entice agonistics like myself, starting with the fact that wearing them doesn’t make you feel like you’re in an episode of Black Mirror. They are, for all intents and purposes, a pair of slick dark glasses. They still have the noticeable bulge of a VR device, but they’re more along the lines of X-Men’s Cyclops than Johnny Mnemonic . These streamlined shades feature a cable leading to a “puck” the size of an iPhone, a battery-and-computer pack you can place in your pocket or handbag, or clip to your belt. Its 45W fast-charging will probably come in handy, since it only holds enough juice for three hours of continuous playback, but the dangling accessory isn’t too obtrusive a trade-off, given the device’s larger, heavier predecessors. The glasses themselves weigh only about a hundred grams — a quarter of a pound — compared to the five to six hundred grams of the Meta Quest. The biggest upgrade from the Meta Quest, however, is the complete lack of hand-held controllers and the reliance on physical gestures instead. Apple’s equivalent already has this, but the Meta VR Glasses offer the chance to use these flicks and pinches without feeling like you’re in a Saw trap. The initial adjustments seem pretty easy, between switchable nose pads of different sizes and lenses you can slide left and right to ensure they’re at the correct distance. There’s no official info on what to do if you wear glasses just yet, but some leaks out there suggest prescription lens capability is the plan. Tiny cameras alongside the glasses' stems capture minor movements, like using your thumb to imitate scrolling on a touch remote, or pinching an invisible button, which in turn trigger and toggle menus affixed to the space around you. The cameras on the front re-create your regular vision, with a bit of a catch. The world around you gets noticeably noisier (as in, filled with digital noise) and the frame rate doesn’t exactly sync up with fluorescent lightbulbs, so you might see a bit of a flicker when looking past the floating UX at actual surfaces. Navigating the real world will still probably be a challenge, and the tech’s hologram features (and spatial audio) for video calling weren’t part of the demo. However, Meta VR Glasses feel aimed at sitting down to watch movies and TV rather than augmenting reality. With its 5K display made of micro OLED panels, 37 pixels per degree, and Dolby Vision enhancements, you’re getting a pretty high-quality image, and navigating it is gamified too. Once you sync your eye movements to the cursor, simply looking at an app icon will light it up. Just pinch to select. But what about the actual offerings? Well, that’s where things get interesting. In addition to all your streaming favorites (Prime Video, YouTube, DIRECTV, AMC+, Crunchyroll, Plex, and vitally, Tubi), Meta has teamed up with IMAX to bring the world of full-frame, 1:43:1 IMAX movies to your headset. Currently, this is poised to be the only way to watch something like The Odyssey in its native aspect ratio outside of a handful of cinemas. Sadly, that option wasn’t available during our limited tech demo, but it sets Meta VR Glasses apart even from Blu-ray and UHD, which only expand to the size of your HD television — a paltry 16:9. With films like The Odyssey , Sinners and Dune: Part Three reflecting an increased demand for the format, which can’t fully be met, this is the next best thing. But what does actually watching a movie in one of these look like? Well, you have a couple of options. For most films, a screen pops up at a certain distance, which you’ll eventually be able to move back or forth. This feature wasn’t yet available, leaving part of the screen outside the glasses’ field of view, which isn’t ideal, but it’s still early days since the product is several months away from release. Your second option, for select films and experiences, is an “Immersive Cinema” virtual reality viewing room by ILM, built in sync with the movie itself. For this Disney+ demo, I picked Avengers: Infinity War — specifically, the scene where Thor harnesses the power of a dying star to forge his new hammer, Stormbreaker. If you’ve ever fantasized about watching a movie while seated in a grungy space factory as lava splashes from around the screen, you’re in luck. For Marvel and Star Wars offerings, environments like Tatooine and Avengers Tower appear to be in the works. The 3D isn’t too bad either (as evidenced by a short clip of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness), though the effect is no more or less immersive than most current 3D television sets. Upon launch, 3D offerings will be available from the likes of HBO Max, Paramount+ and Peacock. However, where things get really novel is the switch from movies to sports, where you have the option of not just watching your game of choice with a 180-degree field of view — in this case, Game 4 of the 2026 NBA finals; go Knicks — but sitting in a variety of courtside seats and glancing around. This isn’t magic; the folks at Meta had cameras appropriately placed to capture the effect, so future games will have to be equipped for this sort of broadcast if you want to, say, wave at Spike Lee as he jumps around euphorically. Then again, between the NBA finals and the FIFA World Cup, if this summer has proved anything, it’s that sports are a social event, so closing yourself off this way might at best be a backup for plans that fall through. The speakers on the glasses — which you can control using tiny buttons along the bottoms of the stems — provide a fairly immersive surround sound experience courtesy of Dolby Atmos. This comes in handy for playing music-based games like Beat Saber, one of 75 built-in games available at launch (this particular version was enhanced for the device’s handsfree capabilities) in addition to the XBOX Cloud Gaming, i.e. streaming games directly to your headset. You also have the option of scrolling social media, and typing on a nifty keyboard projected on flat surfaces in front of you, as you look down at your digital ghost hands and their spectral glow. The novelty will probably wear off after a while, but at first, it’s pretty thrilling if you’ve never used this kind of technology before — which appears to be the target market for Meta VR Glasses. Of course, there’s a work capability too; you can mirror your Mac or PC into this virtual space, either wirelessly or via USB-C. On the other hand, the device’s $1,299.99 price tag — more than a solid TV and Blu-ray player combined — might be a deterrent to the average consumer who hasn’t yet dipped their toe into VR. That is, unless Meta plans to roll out highly involved tech demos for every potential buyer. The only way to be remotely convinced of the technology is to experience it for yourself, which a re-creation on a flat screen (say, a YouTube video) can’t fully convey. There’s a candy store feeling to wearing one of these and turning around to see a fully (or semi) rendered space behind you, waiting to be filled. There are kinks that still need to be worked out by launch, like the glare from light sources behind you leaking into your field of view (perhaps the one downside to opening up those goggles), but a head tilt here or there can probably solve that issue. Also not part of the tech demo was the ability to re-orient where exactly in your horizontal field of view a given screen appears, but this was something Meta’s engineers demonstrated for us on the fly, with the promise that we’d eventually be able to do it ourselves. Much like legs in the Metaverse, it’s coming, baby. Look, it can be hard to trust big tech in our increasingly dystopian world, and who knows what data this particular chapter of the company will try to harness or sell. But the lineup of streaming services and viewing features on offer makes Meta VR Glasses one of the more intriguing developments in the field if you’re unsure about stepping into virtual spaces. Compared to existing devices on the market, the openness of the design — which still allows you to peek out from time to time and go back to the real world pretty easily — makes for the kind of compromise that fence-sitters like myself might just be able to accept. If nothing else, it’s more convenient, and slightly less embarrassing, than buying a scalped IMAX ticket on eBay.

So we have built a new kind of VR device that delivers the same magical feeling of presence and immersion with high-resolution displays and views of the world around you in a form factor that is a pair of glasses for the first time.” The company says that the glasses are five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3 — and they look much more like normal glasses than the bulky headsets that Meta previously released. Made of magnesium alloy, the glasses are powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite processor. They are powered by a computing puck, which also acts as their battery. Presumably, a user can just slip the puck into their pocket, which allows the glasses to be used on the go. The glasses are largely entertainment-focused and come with micro-OLED panels built into the lenses, which provide a 5K Infinite Display with 37 pixels per degree, as well as Dolby Vision and support for Dolby Atmos audio. Users will be able to download and watch movies. Perhaps one of the more unique features of the glasses, however, is that Meta is pitching them as a great way to enjoy IMAX-captured films. Indeed, the company calls the glasses the “first IMAX Enhanced certified VR device ever.” What does that mean? Meta maintains that their glasses will be one of the only ways to experience the expanded aspect ratio that defines the distinct high-resolution viewing experience. Meta says that it has teamed up with Disney and that, in November, Disney+ users will be able to stream specific movies — including certain Marvel movies — in 3D. Meta says that users will be able to watch specific movies and have their surroundings “transformed with immersive environments, dynamic effects, stunning 3D visuals, and spatial audio” — essentially converting the movie into a VR gaming-type experience. The glasses will also come with Meta AI — its automated virtual assistant — built in, which means that users will be able to talk to the glasses and automate various tasks via voice command. For instance, Meta says you’ll be able to start a movie just by asking your glasses to do so. Other ways to issue commands include hand gestures.
